## c3649bc17348

**Classification: reproduced rival-coverage gap, not demonstrated bad default labels.**

Checked 300 default draws, all three canonical labeled pairs, 60 generated examples
with actual Racket execution, and the exact mixed-length counterexample below.
Source SHA256 is `40e901000923424737230d04eb7ee02c239c5186941e4dd1a22684facf2be3f3`.

The intended rule changes the center of an **exact length-three** vertical green
run to yellow and leaves longer runs unchanged. Rival: recolor the center of
every length-three sliding window, even inside a longer green run. That rival
matches all 3/3 canonical pairs and 60/60 tested default Racket outputs; all 300
sampled default grids contain only exact-three green runs.

Exact 7x8 input (0 background, 3 green, 4 yellow):

```text
00000000
03030300
03030300
03030300
00030300
00000300
00000000
```

Actual Racket output:

```text
00000000
03030300
04030300
03030300
00030300
00000300
00000000
```

Sliding-window rival output:

```text
00000000
03030300
04040400
03040400
00030400
00000300
00000000
```

The reference changes only (2,1). The rival additionally changes (2,3), (3,3),
(2,5), (3,5), and (4,5). This disagreement was executed and retained, not inferred
from source comments. The current self-check rejects the input because it contains
two non-triplet components and only one exact triplet. Thus a negative validation
fixture alone would not teach the intended distinction: a lawful mixture of
positive exact-three objects with four/five-cell distractor runs should be emitted
as a labeled lesson, after domain policy is confirmed by the owner. This is a
recommendation about useful coverage; no admission or training-gain claim is made.
